p1.title: Land Scarcity and Housing Supply Elasticities in Dense Cities
p1.one_line_finding: Supply elasticity is roughly one-third lower in land-constrained cities.

summary.research_question: How responsive is new housing supply to price changes when developable land is scarce?
summary.data: Panel of 120 cities, 2000–2020; permits, prices and satellite-derived land availability.
summary.methodology: Instrumental-variables estimation using exogenous variation in land availability.
main_findings: Supply elasticity is about one-third lower in the most land-constrained cities.
Price effects of demand shocks are correspondingly larger.
sub_findings: Height limits account for roughly half the gap.
Effects are larger for owner-occupied than rental stock.
summary.relevance: Directly informs assumptions on how quickly supply can respond to demand shocks.

singapore.criterion: Includes Singapore in the cross-city sample.

p2.title: Public Housing Allocation and Household Wealth: Evidence from Singapore
p2.one_line_finding: Earlier allocation raises household net wealth at retirement.

summary.research_question: Does earlier access to public housing change long-run household wealth?
summary.data: Anonymised administrative records of flat allocations, 1995–2015 (sample description only).
main_findings: Earlier allocation increases net wealth at retirement.
summary.relevance: Evidence on the wealth effects of allocation rules under review.

p3.title: Zoning, Density and Prices: A Structural Approach

summary.research_question: How much do zoning limits raise housing prices?
main_findings: Zoning explains a large share of price differences across cities.
summary.relevance: Framework could be adapted to evaluate plot-ratio policy.

p4.title: Public Rental Housing and Mobility in Hong Kong

summary.research_question: Does public rental tenancy reduce job mobility?
sub_findings: Effect is smaller near mass-transit stations.
summary.relevance: Mobility side-effects of public housing design.

singapore.comparability: Dense city-state with a large public housing sector and a similar transit-oriented urban form.
singapore.differences: Hong Kong public housing is mostly rental; Singapore's is mostly owner-occupied leasehold, so the incentives to stay put differ.
singapore.one_line: Tier 2: Hong Kong (rental vs Singapore ownership)

summary.research_question: How do moving costs affect job matching?
main_findings: High moving costs lower match quality.
